images.caption: Figure 1:Efficient reasoning training reduces CoT faithfulness but largely preserves monitorability.(1)We train models with three methods that reward CoT length differently.(2)Then we measure whether the CoT predicts the model’s answers on related inputs (faithfulness) and whether it reveals when an intervention influenced the answer (monitorability).(3)In this example, a∼\sim70% shorter CoT loses faithfulness due to output inconsistency, while monitorability is unchanged.

Figure 2:How we measure faithfulness and monitorability.For faithfulness, a predictor sees the reference model’s answer and CoT on an original input, and predicts the model’s answer on a similar counterfactual input. NSG quantifies how much having the CoT raises the predictor’s accuracy compared to not having the CoT(Mayne et al., 2026). For monitorability, an intervention changes the model’s answer, and a monitor reading only the CoT must detect this influence(Guan et al., 2025).
